newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end slightly lower, H&M plunges.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end slightly lower, H&M plunges.

text.p: Swedish share prices closed slightly lower on Thursday as some blue chips fell.
The Stockholm bourse's general index fell 0.16 percent to 2,842.58 in turnover of 5.45 billion crowns.

Fashion retailer Hennes & Maurtiz was in the limelight after a decision to transfer its shares from the stock market's main A list to the smaller O list for tax reasons. The share plunged 19.5 crowns to 234.5.
"Overseas portfolio administrators cannot own O-listed shares without special permission," said one broker, adding that many foreigners held stakes in the group.
Dealers were split about what direction the share would take in the future.
Heavyweights drugs group Astra and automotive group Volvo slid. Astra fell two crowns to 128 while Volvo dropped five crowns to 210.5.
Telecoms group Ericsson rose four crowns to 281.5, in line with its U.S. performance early in the Thursday session.

The construction sector was a winner, up 1.90 percent after Nackebro's bid for Fabege in wake of a rival bid by Hufvudstaden. Nackebro rose 1.5 crowns to 100.5. Fabege ended flat at 84 after jumping 10 on Wednesday.
Car safety equipment maker Autoliv fell four crowns to 308 in a correction after a couple of days of sharp gains.
